Order
With consent heard finally.
2.  The applicant has filed this first bail application u/S.439 Cr.P.C for grant of bail.

Applicant has been arrested on 18/1/2024 by Police Station Mahila Thana Mandla in connection with Crime No.04/2024 registered for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366A, 376, 365, 370, 506, 34 of IPC, Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act and 3(1)(w)(i), 3(2)(V) of the ST SC Act.
3. It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is suffering confinement since 18/1/2024 and charge-sheet has already been filed.
Therefore, chance of tempering with evidence/ witness is remote.
It is further submitted that allegations of rape is attributable over co-accused Dharmendra and not over present applicant.

He Sonu Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18050232/
1 runs a recruitment agency where he employed complainant and other girls for domestic work.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He fairly submits that girls employed may not be major and may be minor but certainly allegations of rape or pushing the girls into flesh trade does not appear to be attributable prima facie.
He does not bear any criminal record.
Confinement amounts to pretrial detention.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial and he would not be a source of embarrassment and harassment to the complainant party in any manner.
Under these circumstances, counsel prayed for grant of bail to the applicant.

4. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer on the ground that the applicant is resident of Agra (U.P.) and chance of absconsion cannot be ruled out and she prayed for dismissal of this application.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the submission and the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties, but without commenting on the merits of the case, it is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.
Out of these two sureties one shall be cash surety and another shall be local surety of State of M.P.
In case of any violation of bail conditions, cash surety shall be immediately forfeited.

sentences.text: (viii) The applicant shall not try to contact the complainant in person, through electronic mode or through somebody else otherwise benefit of bail shall immediately be withdrawn.
(ix) The applicant shall mark his presence on first Sunday of every second month (alternate month) between 10 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. at concerned Police Station till conclusion of trial.

7. At this stage, this Court deems fit to invoke the concept of "Shaurya Didi" which is being discussed and conceptualized in the Juvenile Justice Committee Meeting, held at Bhopal on 23rd July, 2022,
where Judges and Executives (as committee members) given approval to this concept.

In pursuance thereof, Gwalior bench of this Court has passed certain orders time and again whereby a woman Sub Inspector Police or woman Police Constable is being appointed as "Shaurya Didi" for a girl, who is in need of Care and Protection.
In the present case, the victims are minor girls and are juvenile.
Therefore, they are in need of Care and Protection by the society and by the State as well.

Therefore,
Superintendent of Police and Collector Mandla are directed to look into this matter personally and appoint any woman Sub Inspector of Police Station Mahila Police Thana of Mandla as "Shaurya Didi"
for taking care of victims of the case.

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Police Thana of Mandla
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Duty of "Shaurya Didi" would be to Mentor,
Guide and Encourage those girls, so that, they can absorb the shock inflicted because of present incident and they would be empowered to look forward for better future.
They may be encouraged to complete their education and involve in other creative pursuits.
That Woman Officer (Shaurya Didi) would regularly keep those girls in touch through mobile phone and would visit frequently say once in a week or ten days.
So that, she can assure those minor girls about their safety and security.

8. Hopefully, Collector Mandla would give necessary instructions to District Woman and Child Empowerment Officer in this regard and Superintendent of Police Mandla shall appoint a suitable Woman Police Officer as "Shaurya Didi" and would keep personal track over the progress of victims.
9. Application stands allowed and disposed of.

10. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court as well as Collector and Superintendent of Police,
Mandla for information and compliance.
Certified copy as per rules/directions.

(ANAND PATHAK) JUDGE m/-
